title: Crime and law — core set
titleVi: Tội phạm và pháp luật — bộ từ cốt lõi
description: Bộ từ về hình phạt, tái hoà nhập và cách hệ thống tư pháp vận hành. Đây là nhóm từ giúp bạn bàn luận về trừng phạt và phòng ngừa tội phạm một cách có chiều sâu.
ieltsUse: Dùng cho Task 2 các đề về hình phạt, tù giam hay cải tạo, tội phạm vị thành niên, an ninh mạng và vai trò của cộng đồng trong phòng chống tội phạm.

words.def: something that discourages people from committing an offence
words.example: Longer sentences are widely assumed to act as a deterrent, yet evidence is mixed.

words.def: to discourage someone from doing something by fear of consequences
words.example: Visible policing is more likely to deter petty crime than sporadic crackdowns.

words.vi: án treo, phóng thích có điều kiện
words.def: release of a prisoner before the end of their sentence
words.example: Prisoners granted parole must report to a supervisor for several years.

words.def: the tendency of released offenders to commit further crimes
words.example: Vocational training in prisons has cut recidivism by almost a third in some countries.

words.def: the state of being kept in prison
words.example: The cost of incarceration per prisoner now exceeds the cost of a university place.

words.vi: án tù, hình phạt giam giữ
words.def: a punishment that involves time in prison
words.example: Judges impose a custodial sentence only when community penalties are inadequate.

words.def: unpaid work ordered as an alternative to prison
words.example: Offenders sentenced to community service often repair public spaces and graffiti.

words.def: a period of supervision instead of a prison sentence
words.example: Young offenders are frequently placed on probation and required to meet a caseworker.

words.def: law-breaking by children or teenagers
words.example: Youth clubs in deprived districts have reduced juvenile delinquency noticeably.

words.def: an illegal act or crime
words.example: First-time offenders often commit a minor offence under peer influence.

words.def: a person who has committed a crime
words.example: Rehabilitation programmes help first-time offenders return to work after release.

words.def: minor offences such as shoplifting or vandalism
words.example: Foot patrols have cut petty crime in the city centre by a quarter.

words.def: the crime of deceiving someone for financial gain
words.example: Online fraud targets elderly people who are less familiar with digital banking.

words.def: the police and other agencies that apply the law
words.example: Effective law enforcement depends on public trust, not only on tougher penalties.

words.vi: cơ quan xét xử, hệ thống thẩm phán
words.def: the system of courts and judges in a country
words.example: An independent judiciary is essential if citizens are to challenge the state.

words.def: the decision reached by a court
words.example: The verdict was appealed because key forensic evidence had been mishandled.

words.def: an act of breaking a law or agreement
words.example: Any breach of parole conditions results in an immediate return to prison.

words.def: the death penalty
words.example: Capital punishment has been abolished in the great majority of European states.

words.def: a prison sentence lasting until the offender dies
words.example: Murderers may still receive life imprisonment without any possibility of parole.

words.def: illegal or dishonest behaviour
words.example: Whistle-blowers who report corporate wrongdoing deserve legal protection.

words.vi: lệnh giới nghiêm, lệnh cấm ra đường
words.def: an order keeping people off the streets at certain hours
words.example: Some parents impose a curfew to keep teenagers away from late-night pubs.

words.vi: hành vi phá hoại tài sản công
words.def: deliberate damage to public property
words.example: Better street lighting has reduced vandalism in the neighbourhood considerably.

words.def: crime committed using computers or the internet
words.example: Cybercrime crosses borders, so national police forces struggle to investigate it.

words.def: physical or emotional abuse within a household
words.example: Refuges for victims of domestic violence are still desperately underfunded.

words.vi: công lý phục hồi (hoà giải nạn nhân - người phạm tội)
words.def: a system that focuses on repairing harm rather than imposing punishment
words.example: Restorative justice gives victims a direct voice, which many find more satisfying than a court verdict.
